comments: Fiber-supported heptane droplet burning in a 0.20/0.45/0.25 O2/N2/CO2, 0.70 atm ambient environment. The droplet ignites and shortly after ignition a small droplet or debris ignites to the W (color camera) or N (LLUV) of the droplet. This small droplet/particle burns for only a short time. It is not visible in the HiBMS. The droplet burns for only a short time before radiatively extinguishing. There is continued rapid vaporization after visible flame exinction, followed by avapor cloud formation approximately 5 seconds after visible flame extinction. This is an indication of cool flame burning
